reden: Yes. Multiple findings in the audit report precisely describe the same sqrt bug in Float128.sol’s high-precision (Uint512) branch: after computing rMan, the code performs the 73-digit overflow adjustment (rMan /= 10; ++rExp) before halving the exponent (rExp = rExp/2), which yields an off-by-one exponent and returns a result 10x too small for affected large inputs. The report cites the exact code path, mechanism, impact, and even suggests equivalent fixes (halve first or add +2 before halving). This matches H-01’s description and proposed diff (move halving before the 72→73 digit adjustment). Fixing the report’s issue would fix H-01 and vice versa.
